steps.content: The skyraft consumes all the remaining Dragonstones at last. The crew has no choice but to get off and continue moving toward the target with the Prism Light's aid.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I've been wondering, why do you all dress so lightly? Shouldn't you wear protective clothing?
You've had this question in your mind since early on, but you only ask it now to ease the somewhat heavy mood among the crew.

steps.speaker: Tierney
steps.content: You think I get cold this easily? Remember who dug you out of the avalanche?
Tierney shifts out of the Prism Light's protection and grabs the ice flakes flying in the sky. Even the extreme cold doesn't slow her down.
The ice flakes gather in her hands to form an icicle so deep blue it's almost inky. Tierney gestures to you with it.

steps.speaker: Tierney
steps.content: Can... you... feel... it?
Her voice sounds dragged, the drawl streaming into your ears slowly. Then, she throws the dark-blue icicle outside unhurriedly.
You feel slightly helpless, but you can't stop Tierney.

steps.speaker: Tierney
steps.content: Have you been to Welkin City? It was the largest city on the Isle of Sky. That's where you found the newest inventions and the most exciting stuff.
You shake your head, unsure why Tierney suddenly brings up the ruins of Welkin City. Staring at the Blessing Sun, she seems to lapse into a certain memory.

steps.speaker: Tierney
steps.content: Everything from children's toys to armor used for mining minerals, you could find the best models in Welkin City. They even had a plan to raise Welkin City right under the Blessing Sun so that it could be rid of the Ice Plague's threat forever.

steps.speaker: Tierney
steps.content: But it was all ruined when the Ice Plague suddenly struck the city.

steps.speaker: Tierney
steps.content: <size=32>The machines and buildings were frozen. So were the people. Some survived with the power in their blood as the Dragon's Children, but that's the most unfortunate ending. If frozen by the Ice Plague, their minds and actions became a thousand time slower.</size>

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Is that worse than being buried under snow?

steps.speaker: Tierney
steps.content: Ha! How are the two things comparable?
Tierney rolls her eyes and continues seriously.

steps.speaker: Tierney
steps.content: To those people, their lives were forever frozen on the day of the disaster. "It's finally here." "Run." "What just happened?"

steps.speaker: Tierney
steps.content: They may have only reached the end of these thoughts today.
Tierney looks around in the darkness. Somehow, you can hear a low whimper in the howling snow.

steps.speaker: Tierney
steps.content: Listen. The ancestors' blood was even stronger. They say these calls from the abyss are the ancestors' greetings to those who risk coming down to the earth, like us.

steps.speaker: Tierney
steps.content: What are they saying? Are they warning us to leave or crying out for help?

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Telling you to hurry up with the journey.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If I were your ancestor, I would tell you to hurry up with the journey and find the Dragon of Genesis instead of wasting your precious energy on spooky tales.

steps.speaker: Tierney
steps.content: Tsk, you just ruined the mood...
(Scene change)
The long journey continues.
The Prism Light flickers, interrupted continuously by the ever-present dark-blue chill. Now you understand that this is no simple snow, but some kind of fatal, special magical power.
The two of you trudge on arduously in the snow. Tierney's breaths become very shallow, something you can tell easily now that her words are also scarce.
On the other hand, the power of your shackles becomes more active in this kind of environment, so you're able to persevere for a bit longer.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: We're not gonna find it if we keep on like this.

steps.speaker: Tierney
steps.content: Shut... Shut your big mouth... Turn up the light, I can't ******* see the way ahead.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: This is already the maximum brightness.

steps.speaker: Tierney
steps.content: Stop... lying...
Tierney reached out a hand, likely to snatch the Prism Light from your hand. But she staggered and fell.
You run over to grab her hand, trying to pull her up.
She's clearly out of strength, yet she still forces herself to go on to guide the way for you.

steps.speaker: Tierney
steps.content: Don't... do that. Don't... waste your power. You've got... more important things to do.
Tierney's hands seem long frozen that she can't even make a small gesture with them. Throughout the journey in this round, you've never seen Tierney this affected by the Ice Plague.
The long darkness seems to have no end. The shackles' power is becoming more active.

A crack appears on the Prism Light's surface, and the white light leaves its constraints like a dancing fairy. The utterly intensified Ice Plague power invades your muscles, bones, and blood, reaching your hearts.

Perhaps with the shackles, you can temporarily stop the Ice Plague from corroding Tierney further, but when you think of the Game Master's sudden intrusion in the last round, you struggle to make a prompt decision.

If Tierney was a puppet or avatar of that Sinner, then perhaps the shackles could reach her through this connection. But if like you, Tierney was only a previous player, then the shackles' effect on her would be hard to foresee.

This is only a test. If you choose wrong this time, you can choose again next time. Isn't this how a game works? You can keep on saving and loading, until you find the only correct solution. Tetya is still alive too, isn't she?

steps.speaker: Tierney
steps.content: Chosen One, it looks like I can't go on further with you... If you can keep going, don't give up.
Her body is already corroded by the snow, her voice slowing down and dragging out. If you have to make a choice, now is your final chance.
You reach out a hand and extend the shackles' power to the core of her heart.

steps.speaker: Tierney
steps.content: Yes... This is my fate... Our fate.
A dark-blue liquid oozing out of her eyes, she's completely corroded by the Ice Plague. The shackles can't stop the Ice Plague from corroding her, but instead provokes that power further.
She's going to die in this round.
[Scene Change]
The dying spirit shrouds your entire world like a thick black mist. Your consciousness staggers on in the mist and finally ends up in an unfamiliar room.
An old fireplace. Stacks of books. A box of tidily organized dice. There's also a sandbox made of paper at the center of the table. You seem to have seen this place.
You reach out to touch the dice on the table tentatively but get pushed away by a mysterious force.
<size=44>Ah!</size>
Startled, you turn to look for the owner of the voice and find her behind the pile of books and sheets.

steps.speaker: Little Girl
steps.content: Let's have one of these, then add one of those. Hahaha, this design is just too fun! Nothing tops this!
A young and small figure squats among a pile of thick rulebooks. She's reading a book while doodling on cardboard, so immersed in her own world that she doesn't notice your presence.
But as she talks, the little girl's voice suddenly dwindles. Staring at the dim light bulb above her head, she mumbles to herself.

steps.speaker: Little Girl
steps.content: When's Grandpa coming back? He promised to play DisChess with me last time. Now even the fifth extension pack is out.
She glimpses at the paper box on the side and draws a small mark on it.

steps.speaker: Little Girl
steps.content: The tenth extension pack. The letter says when the tenth extension pack comes out, he'll be back. Hehe, he'll know nothing by then, I can destroy him in seconds.

steps.speaker: Little Girl
steps.content: Of course, I won't forget about the Isles of Aesthia!
The little girl turns to the sandbox on the table and cackles.

steps.speaker: Little Girl
steps.content: Hehe, rest assured! You'll all appear in Aesthia! Every single one of you!
The girl gently touches the figurines and buildings made out of cardboard and a fine dragon made of metal.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Is she the creator of this world?

steps.content: An answer emerges in your heart.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But... a kid so young, how can she...

steps.speaker: Game Master
steps.content: <color=#7683a2>How can she? I think you underestimate her.</color>
You hear the Game Master's voice genuinely this time. Not in your heart, but from behind you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Are you cheating again?
You turn and finally see her in person for the first time.

steps.speaker: Game Master
steps.content: Oh? But this time... It looks like you're the one cheating instead...

steps.speaker: Game Master
steps.content: Anyway, it doesn't matter. If you can make it here, it means you're different from those other boring players.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What is this place?

steps.speaker: Game Master
steps.content: Is that a question for me? Hehe, take a guess. If you get it right, I'll give you a reward of the hidden route.
She's indeed very childish.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: This is where the world is born.

steps.content: You look at the sandbox in the little girl's hands, watching it change bit by bit. The islands are pieced together. Blue and white paper bits are sprinkled over the sandbox like icing.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Cyrus is just a ploy. You're the ultimate villain in this game, the legendary Dragon of Genesis.

steps.speaker: Game Master
steps.content: You guessed it right, but you also guessed it wrong. In this case, I can only let you take a glimpse of the reward.
She throws out a dark-purple dice. This space made up of memories begins to blur and vanish as the dice spins...
Transition, cut to CG

steps.speaker: Game Master
steps.content: Alright, be it a success or failure, my dear Chosen One, the final game begins now!
The girl's hand reaches down from the sky. You see the whole world rearrange under her touch.
Every rock and every person in this world goes back to their original state under her fingers, except for the dark-blue snow. It covers even more areas now.
